overview: Everest Group, Ltd. is a Bermuda-domiciled global reinsurance and insurance holding company (formerly Everest Re Group, renamed 2023) that has written P&C business since 1973. The company underwrites property, casualty and specialty reinsurance (catastrophe, mortgage, marine, aviation, engineering, professional lines, credit/surety, motor, agriculture/crop, political violence) alongside commercial primary insurance, operating through brokers, ceding companies, wholesale/retail/surplus-lines channels and program administrators across the US, Europe, Bermuda and internationally. Following a 2025 strategic reset that sold the renewal rights to most of its global retail commercial insurance business to AIG, Everest now reports three segments: Reinsurance Treaty, Global Wholesale & Specialty, and Legacy.

business_model.summary: Everest earns underwriting profit (premiums less losses and expenses) plus float income from investing premiums before claims are paid. Reinsurance (treaty and facultative) is the larger, higher-margin engine; primary/specialty insurance adds diversification but has been the source of recent reserve trouble. A large ($40B+) fixed-income-heavy investment portfolio generates meaningful net investment income that has become an increasingly important earnings driver in the higher-rate environment.
business_model.customer_type: B2B — ceding insurance companies and reinsurance brokers (Reinsurance segment); wholesale/retail brokers, surplus lines brokers and program administrators (Insurance segment)
business_model.geographic_mix: US, Bermuda, Europe (Ireland/UK hubs), and international operations; FY2025 gross written premium of $17.7B, 72.4% Reinsurance / 27.1% Insurance

competitive_position.market_position: Top-tier global reinsurer by premium volume, with a hybrid reinsurance/primary-insurance model that differentiates it from pure-play reinsurers (RenaissanceRe) and positions it closer to diversified hybrids like Arch Capital; recently pared back primary retail insurance to refocus on reinsurance and specialty wholesale.

moat_factors.description: $17.7B GWP across property, casualty, specialty and mortgage reinsurance lines provides diversification benefits and large-line capacity that smaller reinsurers cannot match
A+ (AM Best, S&P) / A1 (Moody's) financial strength ratings support participation on large treaties and cat programs requiring highly-rated counterparties
Decades-long relationships with reinsurance brokers and ceding companies support renewal retention, though reinsurance is a largely commoditized, price-competitive market with low switching costs
$40B+ investment portfolio and growing alternative-asset/limited-partnership allocation generate a meaningful and growing float-income advantage

weaknesses: US casualty reserve inadequacy has recurred across 2024-2025, undermining underwriting credibility and drawing negative rating-agency outlook revisions
Reinsurance is a commoditized, cyclical market with limited pricing power versus peers in soft markets
Primary insurance franchise materially shrunk after the AIG renewal-rights sale, reducing diversification and scale in that segment
Smaller and less specialized in property-catastrophe than RenaissanceRe, and less diversified than Berkshire/Munich Re/Swiss Re in non-P&C lines

growth_drivers: Reinsurance Treaty and Global Wholesale & Specialty segments generating strong underwriting income (combined ratio ~90% in core businesses) as the growth engine post-restructuring
Continued growth in net investment income (5-year 2020-2025 CAGR of ~27%) from portfolio growth, higher reinvestment yields, and expanding limited-partnership/alternative returns
Capital release from the AIG retail insurance renewal-rights transaction (~$2B GWP divested) redeployed into higher-return reinsurance/specialty lines and buybacks
Large share buyback program (~73% of shares retired under the long-standing program, cumulative $5.4B+, with a $4.74B authorization) supporting per-share value growth
Potential hard-market pricing in select reinsurance/specialty lines (crop, mortgage, casualty) even as property reinsurance pricing softens
Adverse development cover ($1.2B) and reserve remediation actions aimed at drawing a line under legacy US casualty reserve risk, freeing management focus and capital for core underwriting

business.description: $1.7B of pre-tax adverse reserve development recorded in FY2025 (on top of $1.3B in FY2024) tied to social inflation and excess casualty/liability lines; further charges remain possible despite the new $1.2B ADC
Property reinsurance pricing declined 15-20% at recent renewals amid abundant traditional and alternative capital, pressuring margins into 2027
Sale of retail commercial insurance renewal rights to AIG shrinks the Insurance segment, concentrating the business more heavily in reinsurance cyclicality

financial.description: Large natural catastrophe and man-made loss exposure (e.g., $94M Iran war-related losses in Q2 2026) can produce sharp quarterly earnings swings
$40B+ predominantly fixed-income portfolio is exposed to interest rate moves and credit spread widening; alternative/LP allocations add mark-to-market volatility
Repeated adverse development has pressured ROE and prompted negative outlooks from all three major rating agencies

regulatory.description: Bermuda-domiciled but subject to US, UK/EU (Solvency II-equivalent) and other regulatory capital regimes; AIG renewal-rights transaction required regulatory approvals across multiple regions
AM Best, S&P and Moody's all moved to negative outlooks (Oct 2025) following reserve charges; a downgrade would raise cost of capital and could affect cedent/broker relationships

macro.description: Elevated loss emergence in US excess casualty and liability lines driven by social inflation is a sector-wide trend pressuring reserves industry-wide
Falling rates would reduce reinvestment yields on the large fixed-income book and net investment income growth, a key recent earnings driver
Increasing frequency/severity of secondary perils and named catastrophes raises modeled loss costs across the reinsurance industry

execution.description: CEO Juan Andrade resigned abruptly in January 2025; Jim Williamson (former Group COO) was named acting then permanent CEO — execution risk during a period of major segment restructuring
Recasting into three segments (Reinsurance Treaty, Global Wholesale & Specialty, Legacy) and transitioning retail insurance renewals to AIG through 2026 creates near-term operational complexity

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global reinsurance capacity remains ample (traditional + alternative/ILS capital), softening property-cat pricing after several hard-market years (2023-2024); casualty lines remain firmer but reserve risk (social inflation) is a sector-wide concern into 2026-2027
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — reinsurance pricing and underwriting margins move through multi-year hard/soft cycles driven by catastrophe loss experience and capital flows
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-to-high — large fixed income portfolio; net investment income benefits from higher reinvestment yields, but falling rates or credit spread widening would pressure both NII and portfolio marks
key_input_costs: Claims/loss cost inflation (social inflation, medical cost trend)

recent_developments.event: CEO Juan C. Andrade resigned effective January 3, 2025; Jim Williamson (Group COO) named acting CEO, then confirmed permanent President & CEO later in January 2025

Everest announced sale of renewal rights to the majority of its global retail commercial insurance business (~$2B GWP) to AIG, covering US, UK, European and Asia-Pacific operations, effective transition through Q1 2026
Everest secured a $1.2 billion Adverse Development Cover reinsurance agreement protecting North America Insurance liabilities for accident years 2024 and prior
Q3 2025: $361M of prior-year US casualty reserve strengthening (accident years 2022-2024); AM Best revised outlook to negative on Everest Group and subsidiaries

Full-year 2025 results: $17.7B gross written premium, Group combined ratio 98.6% (Reinsurance 91.7%, Insurance 114.6%), net income $1.6B; FY2025 total adverse reserve development of $1.7B pre-tax ($1.28B Insurance, $684M Reinsurance)
Segments recast into Reinsurance Treaty, Global Wholesale & Specialty, and Legacy in connection with 10-K recast/8-K filing

Q2 2026 operating EPS of $14.85 beat consensus by ~1.8%; core businesses (Reinsurance Treaty + Global Wholesale & Specialty) posted $317M underwriting income on a 90% combined ratio; GWP in core businesses down ~7% YoY on deliberate underwriting discipline amid softening property pricing; $94M of Iran war-related losses recorded; over $470M returned to shareholders in the quarter

items.notes: Management reiterated focus on underwriting quality over volume; core (ex-Legacy) businesses posted a 90% combined ratio in Q2 2026

Management guided to continued premium discipline given softening property reinsurance pricing (down 15-20% at recent renewals) and reduced US casualty exposure; expects competitive conditions to persist into 2027

items.target: Continued aggressive buybacks and dividends (~9% capital return yield run-rate)
items.notes: $4.74B buyback authorization outstanding; ~73% of historical share count retired cumulatively (~$5.4B+ spent); quarterly dividend of $2.00/share ($8.00 annualized)

items.target: No explicit new charge guided, but cautious outlook maintained
items.notes: Management emphasized reserve remediation actions (ADC, re-underwriting) are intended to reduce — but not eliminate — the risk of further adverse development in US excess casualty/liability lines

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Jim Williamson has emphasized a pivot toward underwriting profitability over premium growth, citing disciplined pricing and reduced US casualty exposure as central to restoring investor confidence after two consecutive years of adverse reserve development. Management highlighted strong core-business underwriting income (90% combined ratio) and robust net investment income as offsetting softer top-line growth, while flagging that property reinsurance pricing softness is expected to persist through 2027.

bull_case: Core reinsurance and specialty businesses are demonstrating strong underwriting discipline (~90% combined ratio) even as the company sheds lower-return retail insurance exposure

Aggressive capital return program (large buyback authorization, ~9% capital return yield, growing dividend) directly supports per-share value creation, especially with the stock trading at a single-digit trailing P/E
Growing net investment income (27% 5-yr CAGR) from a large, growing investment portfolio provides a diversified, less-volatile earnings stream that cushions underwriting cycle swings
AIG renewal-rights transaction and $1.2B adverse development cover are concrete steps to de-risk the legacy US casualty book and free capital for higher-return reinsurance underwriting
Strong balance sheet and financial strength ratings (A+/A1, albeit negative outlook) support participation in large treaties and preserve franchise value with cedents and brokers
bear_case: Two consecutive years of material US casualty adverse reserve development ($1.3B in FY2024, $1.7B in FY2025) raise doubts about reserve adequacy and management's ability to accurately price long-tail casualty risk

All three major rating agencies (AM Best, S&P, Moody's) moved to negative outlooks in October 2025, raising the risk of an actual downgrade that would increase cost of capital and pressure competitive standing
Softening property reinsurance pricing (down 15-20% at recent renewals, expected to persist into 2027) combined with deliberately shrinking premium volume signals a period of top-line contraction
Loss of scale/diversification in primary insurance following the AIG renewal-rights sale narrows the business mix and increases relative dependence on the more cyclical reinsurance segment

Catastrophe and geopolitical loss volatility (e.g., $94M Iran-related war losses in Q2 2026) demonstrates continued exposure to unpredictable, large single-event losses that can disrupt quarterly earnings
Recent CEO transition (Andrade's abrupt January 2025 resignation) occurred amid the reserve and strategic-restructuring turmoil, adding execution risk during a critical repositioning period
